top.title: When do the Lions get to Germany? Dan Campbell details travel plans
top.description: The Detroit Lions are all business as they prepare for an overseas flight to Munich, Germany, for an international game with the New England Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 15. Lions coach Dan Campbell relayed the team's plans for the trip, including how they'll deal with practice, when they'll make the flight, and how they'll handle the acclimation process upon arrival, during his weekly radio interview with Costa & Jansen with Heather on 97.1 The Ticket. Campbell said the travel is "not going to" impact the team as they look to make it five straight wins against the reigning AFC champion. "We're gonna practice our tails off [Wednesday] and Thursday. We're gonna take a shower. We're gonna jump on this freaking plane. We're gonna take a nap, and then we're going to wake up, we're going to meet, and we're going to walk-through red-zone practice," Campbell said. "We're gonna stay up for another four or five hours later than normal. We're gonna wake up, go full speed for about 45 minutes the day before the game. They're going to walk around a little bit, enjoy the sights, get a good sleep. We're going to wake up and be ready to play. "And then we're going to jump on the plane, get ready for Tampa (Bay in Week 11), and be ready for that game, too. Then we're going to be ready for the Chicago Bears, Thanksgiving, at our place. We're gonna be ready to go." More: Detroit Lions trade deadline tracker: Latest news, updates More: Lions finalize trade to land safety Andre Cisco from Jets The Patriots (5-4) will be highly motivated coming off a devastating 45-27 home loss to the Green Bay Packers. New England has had an up-and-down season since last year's Super Bowl appearance, but Campbell expects coach Mike Vrabel to have his guys ready for the trip in a game the Patriots need to win after losing two of their last three. Campbell said the Patriots' performance against Green Bay "is not a good snapshot of what New England is." "This team plays hard, man. It's a talented unit," Campbell said. nbianchi@detroitnews.com @nolanbianchi This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: When do the Lions get to Germany? Dan Campbell details travel plans

top.title: ‘I will be number one P4P’: David Benavidez focused for Cieslak challenge
top.description: David Benavidez says that becoming undisputed champ at cruiserweight is “inevitable,” as he prepares to face Michal Cieslak with three title belts on the line on December 5 at home in Arizona. But Benavidez doesn’t want to limit the vision to just becoming an undisputed champion. He’s also looking to be seen as the world’s best boxer, bar none. “I got two belts in my first fight at cruiserweight and now I’m going for a third,” Benavidez said. “Me being undisputed is inevitable. I’m going to make my way to the top of the pound-for-pound list very soon. I will be number one.” Benavidez (32-0, 26 KO) dominated Gilberto “Zurdo” Ramirez to win the WBA and WBO cruiserweight titles on May 2 in Las Vegas, and will be trying to add the WBC belt currently held by Cieslak (28-2, 22 KO), who comes over from Poland as a heavy underdog. “The biggest challenge with Cieslak is that he’s coming into this fight defending his title for the first time,” Benavidez said. “Every fighter has that motivation after winning the title that you really don’t wanna let it go. He’s gonna come in strong, but I don’t run away from any competition.”

top.title: McIlroy’s Take On Recent DQ Shows Rules Must Change
top.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy labeled Frank Kennedy’s disqualification from Q-School as “harsh” but backed the need for stricter behavior rules. The 21-year-old Manchester native lost his chance at a DP World Tour card after swinging a putter in anger on the 11th hole. GolfMagic reported that officials deemed the outburst as “serious misconduct” following the incident at the Infinitum Resort in Spain. Kennedy missed a birdie putt and damaged the green while walking to the next hole. The Incident and the Reaction Kennedy’s actions sparked immediate debate across the tour. American golf journalist Ryan French first broke the news that Kennedy and his father begged rules officials to review the decision. The young golfer released a statement late Monday claiming he did not understand why the penalty was so severe. “I have always respected and followed the Rules of Golf,” he said. Kennedy added that many senior players he spoke to were surprised by the ruling. He noted, “If accidental contact like this, repaired at once, is a disqualification offence, I will respect that.” McIlroy addressed the situation while preparing for the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. He told reporters that the situation seemed very unfortunate. The Northern Irishman discussed the incident with his caddie Harry Diamond out on the course. McIlroy stated, “It seems harsh but at the same time, I think it’s good that golf and the authorities are cracking down on things like this.” He called it an “unbelievably unfortunate incident” but supported the crackdown on misconduct. A New Era of Discipline Governing bodies for the four men’s majors have agreed to clamp down on bad behavior. This shift follows several high-profile incidents during this year’s major championships. At Augusta National, Sergio Garcia drove his club into the tee box and a water cooler. Scotland’s Robert MacIntyre directed a middle finger at the 15th green after a quadruple-bogey. Both players received reprimands for their actions. Jon Rahm also faced a warning for tossing his club at the Open at Royal Birkdale. He briefly “forgot” about the new code of conduct, the Spaniard confessed. Joaquin Niemann earned the distinction of being the first player penalized with shot deductions for this mid-round. The governing bodies want to protect the image of the sport. They will not tolerate outbursts that damage the course or disrespect the game. top.title: Kyle Hamilton joins kids from Boys & Girls Club for football and learning
top.description: Kyle Hamilton’s latest community appearance connected his childhood experience with an opportunity to support Baltimore youth. The Ravens safety and Team Toyota athlete joined elementary school teacher Mary Crippen, creator of NFeLementary, for an afternoon of football-themed learning and games at the Baltimore Ravens Boys & Girls Club. Both grew up participating in Boys & Girls Clubs, giving the event a personal connection beyond their shared interest in football. The gathering took place Monday during Baltimore’s extended break between games. Toyota brought Hamilton and Crippen together to connect with local club members through activities designed to make learning engaging and accessible. Kyle Hamilton shares a connection with club members The program paired NFL-themed games and trivia with the Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Baltimore’s emphasis on academic success, healthy lifestyles, and leadership development. Hamilton brought the perspective of an NFL player who once attended a club himself. Crippen brought her experience using football to engage elementary school students through NFeLementary, combining her work in education with the sport’s ability to capture children’s attention. Their backgrounds gave the gathering a connection to the opportunities Boys & Girls Clubs provide. For Hamilton, participating meant returning to an organization that shaped his upbringing while spending time with children in the community where he now plays. The activities offered another way to connect football with learning, using the game as an entry point for participation and curiosity. Bringing an athlete and an educator together also connected two different approaches to encouraging young people. Ravens touchdowns support Baltimore youth programs The event was part of Toyota’s broader community involvement surrounding football. Toyota, the NFL’s official automotive partner, also supports local youth through the Ravens Toyota Community Touchdowns Program. Under that initiative, Baltimore-area Toyota dealers will donate $414 to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Baltimore for every Ravens touchdown scored this season, according to the event materials. Those contributions support the organization’s work with local children. Hamilton’s appearance added a personal element to that partnership. Alongside Crippen, he returned as a former club member, with an opportunity to contribute to the next generation's experience. top.title: Mercedes And Williams Tie For Ninth Constructors’ Title In 2026
top.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Mercedes has secured its ninth Constructors’ Championship, tying the record set by Williams. This achievement places the German manufacturer alongside the British team in the history books, behind only Ferrari and McLaren. Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali led the tributes to the team for this major milestone on the track. The win marks a return to the top for Mercedes after a period of struggle. Kimi Antonelli’s record as the youngest ever Drivers’ World Champion coincides with this same season, according to Formula1.com . Winning both titles makes 2026 a historic year for the sport and the Mercedes team. Toto Wolff Joins a Legend The championship victory puts team principal Toto Wolff in rare company. According to Formula 1 Official, his ninth title as a leader draws him level with Sir Frank Williams. Wolff stands alongside Frank in the record books. Domenicali praised the team effort required to reach this point. He stated, “My huge congratulations to everyone at the Mercedes Formula 1 Team on becoming 2026 Constructors’ World Champions. Reaching the summit of Formula 1 is never the achievement of one person alone.” The CEO emphasized that the result came from hundreds of people working together at the factory and the circuit. Every member of the team should feel proud of what they have accomplished this season. Rivals Celebrate Hamilton’s Milestone While the team celebrated, Lewis Hamilton reached a personal milestone with his 400th race start. Fernando Alonso, a rival driver, offered his respects to the veteran on the grid. Alonso noted that Hamilton has had an incredible career in F1, with all 400 races in a very competitive position. Alonso added, “But yes, Lewis obviously has had an incredible career in F1, and 400 races, all of them in a very competitive position. Congratulations to him, and hopefully a good race and a good weekend for him.” The 400 Club is a group that few drivers ever enter. New champion Kimi Antonelli could join that same club as early as 2041. At 24 races a year, the young Italian has a long path ahead if he stays healthy and fast. A New Chapter for the Sport Only Ferrari has more wins with 16, and McLaren sits second with 10. Williams and Mercedes now share the third spot with 9 titles each. Mercedes previously won the title for eight consecutive seasons from 2014 to 2021. The 2026 win breaks a recent run where McLaren claimed the 2024 and 2025 titles. A Mercedes-powered car has secured the championship for the third year in a row. Domenicali concluded the official remarks by noting the significance of the moment. He said, “Mercedes have returned to the very top, and in doing so have written another remarkable chapter in the history of Formula 1.” The wait for another Constructors’ Championship ended last weekend in Sao Paulo.

top.title: Agent confirms Liverpool star is in talks over new deal
top.description: Agent confirms Liverpool star is in talks over new deal Alisson Becker Contract Talks Give Liverpool a Clear Goalkeeping Decision Liverpool have a decision to make on Alisson Becker, and it looks like the process has already started. Early discussions are underway over a new deal for the Brazilian, whose current contract is due to expire next June. That matters, because Alisson remains one of the few players in this squad who can still decide games on his own. Liverpool know it, Alisson knows it, and now his camp have effectively confirmed it in public. Alisson Becker open to Liverpool stay There has been noise around several Liverpool contracts in recent months, including Alexis Mac Allister, but Alisson’s situation is simpler. He wants to stay. His agent, Ze Maria, made that clear, saying to WinWin : “Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.” That is not a deal done, and it is not even close to one yet. Still, when a player is happy, the agent is talking and the club are engaged, it usually means there is something concrete to discuss. Photo: IMAGO Liverpool contract talks hinge on age and value The issue is not quality. Alisson has delivered that for years. The issue is age and cost. He is 34, and Liverpool have not built a reputation for handing major renewals to players in that bracket. Then again, rules in football tend to bend for elite players. Liverpool already made one such call when they renewed Mohamed Salah’s deal in April 2025. Alisson could fall into the same category, particularly if the club believe there is still another season or two of top-level performance there. His current wages are reported at £250,000 per week, which already places him among the top earners in the squad. Any extension would involve another serious financial commitment. That is the real calculation here. Crystal Palace display showed Alisson quality Recent mistakes had raised a few questions, fairly enough, but his display against Crystal Palace was a reminder of why Liverpool have trusted him for so long. He made a series of high-level saves and looked like himself again, calm, sharp and decisive. That is why this conversation is happening. If Alisson were declining badly, there would be no serious debate. Instead, Liverpool are weighing cost against certainty, and in his position certainty carries a premium. Nothing is settled yet. These are early talks. But the signs are positive, and for Liverpool, keeping Alisson Becker may still be the most sensible piece of business available.

top.title: Spain manager’s advice to Lamine Yamal as he backs him to follow in Messi, Ronaldo’s footsteps
top.description: Spain manager’s advice to Lamine Yamal as he backs him to follow in Messi, Ronaldo’s footsteps The Spanish national team have already assembled for the ongoing international break, and Barcelona stars including Joan Garcia, Pedri and Pau Cubarsi have already assembled in Luis de La Fuente’s camp. The big name, Lamine Yamal, has not joined up with some niggling pain in his knee and has been exempted from the team’s first game. He has, however, been called up and is expected to be back for the game against England. It will be a special international break this time around, as it marks the first time both Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo will not be in action after both players announced their international retirements. In that sense, the spotlight will not shine a little bit brighter on the next generation of stars, and Lamine Yamal is one who will hog a major part of that spotlight. De La Fuente’s advice Lamine backed to mark an era in football. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking to the media at a press conference, Spain NT manager Luis de La Fuente was asked if he saw Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe capable of filling the void left by Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirements. “They are going to mark an era in football, for sure,” he began, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . “It is very good for football that there is not only one star who is the reference for everyone,” he added. Speaking on the importance of competition between two top stars, the manager said, “There must be two or three players who are references and who believe in that spirit of joy, of follow-up and what sport is a bit: rivalry, always healthy.” Advice to Lamine Yamal De La Fuente had special advice for Yamal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The coach was then asked what advice he would give to the player who is under his tutelage – Lamine Yamal. “He is a very mature boy for his age, but he needs us to accompany him, like any boy his age who is still training. He is aware,” he began. “In private, he shows you that maturity that I am saying, but outside of that environment you also have to protect yourself and defend yourself from everything around you,” he added. De La Fuente then praised Yamal for how he soaks up pressure and criticism with maturity, saying, “And he does it very well. I admire him because a 19-year-old boy, who endures the media pressure he has endured since he was 16, is not easy. It’s very difficult.” “And he does it with tremendous naturalness. You have to tell him to keep growing, improving and working as he does. This way he will have all the doors open to be a legendary footballer,” he added.

top.title: MultiChoice welcomes NBC directive on content rights
top.description: MultiChoice Group has welcomed a directive by the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) reaffirming regulations governing intellectual property rights and the retransmission of audiovisual content in Nigeria. The directive, issued on November 2, 2026, clarifies that access to another broadcasting operator’s signal does not automatically grant the right to retransmit or commercially redistribute its content. It further stipulates that operators must obtain the necessary rights and authorisations before retransmitting protected content, warning that unauthorised retransmission constitutes a violation of intellectual property rights. Welcoming the directive, Chief Executive Officer of MultiChoice Nigeria, Kemi Omotosho, described the NBC’s clarification as an important step towards protecting content creators and rights-holders and promoting a more orderly and sustainable broadcasting market. Omotosho said a clear and predictable regulatory framework would strengthen the creative ecosystem by encouraging investment in local content and creating long-term value for creators, rights-holders, operators and audiences. “The Group welcomes the NBC’s efforts to provide greater clarity on content rights and retransmission rules in Nigeria. This clarification is an important step towards strengthening the protection of creators and rights-holders and fostering a well-structured and sustainable audiovisual market. “A clear and predictable regulatory framework benefits the entire creative ecosystem, supporting investment in local content and creating long-term value for creators, rights-holders, operators and audiences alike,” she said. MultiChoice said the directive provides important regulatory guidance for the broadcasting industry, reinforcing the need to respect intellectual property rights, promote fair competition and ensure a level playing field for legitimate operators. It added that regulatory clarity was essential to encouraging investment in content creation, supporting the sustainability of the broadcasting industry and strengthening the relationship between creators, rights-holders, broadcasters and audiences. The Group reaffirmed its commitment to protecting intellectual property rights and supporting the sustainable development of Africa’s creative industries. It also pledged to continue working with regulators and industry stakeholders to promote legitimate content distribution and strengthen the long-term sustainability of the audiovisual sector. top.title: Subsidy is not coming back — Tinubu insists
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye President Bola Tinubu has ruled out restoring the fuel subsidy, saying his administration will instead expand support for farmers and invest in education, as he campaigned for re-election in Jigawa State. Tinubu spoke on Tuesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Dutse Township Stadium, as part of the party’s nationwide campaign ahead of the 2027 general election. Addressing the subsidy debate, Tinubu said claims that fuel subsidy returns would return were false, arguing that public resources should be directed towards education and agriculture. “To those who say subsidy is coming back, it’s a lie. Don’t let them lie to you again. It’s not going to come back. We cannot spend the future of our children today and feel that they will grow tomorrow. No, they have to be in school. We have to invest in their education. We have to invest in agriculture,” he said. Tinubu said his administration would subsidise farming and reward small-scale farmers. He promised interest-free loans for farmers and said mechanised farming service centres would be established in six locations. “We will subsidise farming. We will reward small-scale farmers. Interest-free loans for farmers are coming. Prosperity is coming. Food security will happen. I hope you hear me, Jigawa. You hear me, Jigawa. There will be interest-free loans for small-scale farmers. We are going to install a mechanised farming service centre in six geographical locations: mechanised farming,” he said. He also said universities would play a greater role in agricultural research and development. “Our university will be more involved in research and development in agriculture than ever before,” Tinubu said. The president also addressed insecurity, saying his administration had strengthened the police and armed forces and was paying better salaries. “We will conquer insecurity. We’ve been through many wars; we will defeat our enemies, enemies of unity, enemies of stability, and enemies of hope. To assure you that we are doing that, we’ve strengthened the police, we’ve strengthened the armed forces, and we are paying better salaries today,” he added. top.title: Official | Vincent Kompany returns to work at Bayern Munich
top.description: Official | Vincent Kompany returns to work at Bayern Munich Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has taken another significant step towards returning to the touchline following his recent health scare. The Bundesliga champions confirmed on Tuesday that the 40-year-old Belgian has returned to the club’s Säbener Straße training facility. Kompany has been absent from his coaching duties since collapsing while observing a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team on October 23. He was subsequently hospitalised, with further medical examinations reportedly revealing an irritation of the meninges. Bayern have now confirmed that their head coach is recovering and has been back at the club’s training facilities since the beginning of the week. Kompany is also undergoing rehabilitation for a shoulder injury. According to the Münchener Tageszeitung , the Belgian was back working at his office computer by approximately 10 a.m. on Tuesday morning. Vincent Kompany could return after international break Bayern have not yet confirmed when Kompany will resume his responsibilities on the touchline. However, honorary president Uli Hoeneß suggested during an appearance on Bayerischer Rundfunk’s Sonntags-Stammtisch that the coach could return following the November international break. This would potentially put Kompany in contention to oversee Bayern’s Bundesliga encounter with 1. FC Cologne on November 20. In Kompany’s absence, assistant coach Aaron Danks has overseen first-team affairs, with Bayern winning all five competitive fixtures during that period. GGFN | Peter Weis

top.title: NERC approves fresh N30bn for 11 DisCos to provide free meters
top.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved an additional N30 billion for the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) to procure and install free meters for unmetered customers, bringing total approvals under the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF) scheme to N79 billion. The latest approval, which represents the third tranche of the fund, is aimed at accelerating efforts to bridge Nigeria’s metering gap, reduce revenue losses and improve service delivery in the electricity distribution sector. The Commission had earlier approved N21 billion under Tranche A and N28 billion under Tranche B, bringing previous approvals to N49 billion. In Order No. NERC/2026/121, effective November 2, 2026, the regulator said the latest N30 billion would be allocated among the 11 DisCos in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund as of the July 2026 market settlement. According to the order, the funds would be used to meter all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerate the closure of the metering gap among customers classified under Band B. NERC specifically directed the DisCos to deploy the funds for the “procurement and installation of meters for unmetered Band ‘A’ and ‘B’ Customers within their franchise areas.” The intervention comes amid a national metering rate of 63.10 per cent as of August 2026, with 8.05 million of the 12.75 million active electricity customers having meters. Data from the Commission showed that approximately 4.7 million active customers were still without meters. Explaining the objectives of the MAF scheme, NERC said the fund was designed to accelerate meter deployment, close the existing metering gap, reduce commercial and collection losses for DisCos, enhance service quality and improve customer satisfaction. The regulator reiterated that all meters procured and installed under the scheme must be provided to customers free of charge. It stressed that “all meters procured and installed under the MAF framework shall be provided to customers at no cost.” The Commission also directed that every meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. Under the order, the DisCos are required to conduct transparent procurement processes within 10 days to select eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks ready for deployment. top.title: Grêmio aim to clear injury list and keep momentum against the bottom four
top.description: Grêmio aim to clear injury list and keep momentum against the bottom four After securing a place in the Copa do Brasil final and enjoying three days off, Grêmio's squad returns to training this Wednesday (11). Despite the excitement over reaching the final, the club remains on alert as it battles relegation in the Brazilian league. During the international break, the main priority for the medical department and coaching staff is to get injured players fit again, according to ge. Players including Nardoni, Pavon, Danilo Barbosa and Diego Caito will be reassessed over the coming days and could return for the match against Bahia, scheduled for November 18 at the Arena. Another concern is fullback Marlon's fitness. Taken off at halftime in the second leg against Atlético-MG because he could no longer tolerate the pain in his right calf—caused by a knock in the first leg—the player stepped up his physiotherapy sessions last week and is expected to be fully fit when the season resumes. Renato Portaluppi's efforts to shield the squad pay off Besides getting the squad physically fit, coach Renato Portaluppi is working to keep the team's concentration and intensity high. The message within the club is to treat the four remaining Brasileirão fixtures (Bahia, Santos, Corinthians and Mirassol) as cup finals to banish the threat of Série B once and for all. Grêmio sits in 18th place with 37 points, level with Corinthians but behind on goal difference, and just one point behind Internacional, the first team outside the relegation zone. Grêmio's improved performances coincide with the coach's efforts to shield the squad from outside pressure. Before the match against Coritiba on October 26, Renato called on fans to support the team, asked for a pause in the criticism and demanded total focus from his players. The strategy worked: since then, the only defeat came against Flamengo with a reserve side, while the first-choice lineup recorded three wins and a draw. That run secured a place in the Copa do Brasil final and kept alive the dream of qualifying for the Libertadores (provided the club stays in the top flight). nigeria.title: MultiChoice welcomes NBC directive on content rights
nigeria.description: MultiChoice Group has welcomed a directive by the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) reaffirming regulations governing intellectual property rights and the retransmission of audiovisual content in Nigeria. The directive, issued on November 2, 2026, clarifies that access to another broadcasting operator’s signal does not automatically grant the right to retransmit or commercially redistribute its content. It further stipulates that operators must obtain the necessary rights and authorisations before retransmitting protected content, warning that unauthorised retransmission constitutes a violation of intellectual property rights. Welcoming the directive, Chief Executive Officer of MultiChoice Nigeria, Kemi Omotosho, described the NBC’s clarification as an important step towards protecting content creators and rights-holders and promoting a more orderly and sustainable broadcasting market. Omotosho said a clear and predictable regulatory framework would strengthen the creative ecosystem by encouraging investment in local content and creating long-term value for creators, rights-holders, operators and audiences. “The Group welcomes the NBC’s efforts to provide greater clarity on content rights and retransmission rules in Nigeria. This clarification is an important step towards strengthening the protection of creators and rights-holders and fostering a well-structured and sustainable audiovisual market. “A clear and predictable regulatory framework benefits the entire creative ecosystem, supporting investment in local content and creating long-term value for creators, rights-holders, operators and audiences alike,” she said. MultiChoice said the directive provides important regulatory guidance for the broadcasting industry, reinforcing the need to respect intellectual property rights, promote fair competition and ensure a level playing field for legitimate operators. It added that regulatory clarity was essential to encouraging investment in content creation, supporting the sustainability of the broadcasting industry and strengthening the relationship between creators, rights-holders, broadcasters and audiences. The Group reaffirmed its commitment to protecting intellectual property rights and supporting the sustainable development of Africa’s creative industries. It also pledged to continue working with regulators and industry stakeholders to promote legitimate content distribution and strengthen the long-term sustainability of the audiovisual sector. nigeria.title: Subsidy is not coming back — Tinubu insists
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye President Bola Tinubu has ruled out restoring the fuel subsidy, saying his administration will instead expand support for farmers and invest in education, as he campaigned for re-election in Jigawa State. Tinubu spoke on Tuesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Dutse Township Stadium, as part of the party’s nationwide campaign ahead of the 2027 general election. Addressing the subsidy debate, Tinubu said claims that fuel subsidy returns would return were false, arguing that public resources should be directed towards education and agriculture. “To those who say subsidy is coming back, it’s a lie. Don’t let them lie to you again. It’s not going to come back. We cannot spend the future of our children today and feel that they will grow tomorrow. No, they have to be in school. We have to invest in their education. We have to invest in agriculture,” he said. Tinubu said his administration would subsidise farming and reward small-scale farmers. He promised interest-free loans for farmers and said mechanised farming service centres would be established in six locations. “We will subsidise farming. We will reward small-scale farmers. Interest-free loans for farmers are coming. Prosperity is coming. Food security will happen. I hope you hear me, Jigawa. You hear me, Jigawa. There will be interest-free loans for small-scale farmers. We are going to install a mechanised farming service centre in six geographical locations: mechanised farming,” he said. He also said universities would play a greater role in agricultural research and development. “Our university will be more involved in research and development in agriculture than ever before,” Tinubu said. The president also addressed insecurity, saying his administration had strengthened the police and armed forces and was paying better salaries. “We will conquer insecurity. We’ve been through many wars; we will defeat our enemies, enemies of unity, enemies of stability, and enemies of hope. To assure you that we are doing that, we’ve strengthened the police, we’ve strengthened the armed forces, and we are paying better salaries today,” he added. nigeria.title: Video: Noise, mob can’t determine who leads Nigeria – Segalink
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Human rights activist and social commentator, Segun Awosanya, popularly known as Segalink, has said that noise, mob pressure and ethnic sentiments should not determine who becomes Nigeria’s president. Awosanya made the remark during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub, where he spoke about the quality of political candidates and the growing influence of public sentiment in determining political choices ahead of the 2027 general elections. He argued that several capable politicians had been relegated in the country’s political conversations, despite what he described as their leadership qualities and experience. Citing former Minister of Education, Adewole Adebayo, former presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, former Governor of Cross River State, Donald Duke, and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, among others, Awosanya said the country should pay greater attention to the qualities and capacity of its political candidates. “There are other people that we have totally relegated, like I said, that are quality candidates. We have the Adewole of the SDP, we have the Sowores of this world, we have the Donald Duke of this world, we have the Makindes. These are quality people who certain candidates cannot even lace their shoes,” he said. He maintained that political conversations should focus on what candidates intend to do differently for the country rather than the popularity they enjoy or the crowd they command. According to him, Nigerians should not allow what he described as ethnic agendas, mob sentiments and aggressive supporters to dictate the country’s leadership choices. “Let us not look at the noise, the mob, or the crowd, or the irate or virulent people who want to force their way into our hearts, or into our nation for their own ethnic agenda. They should not be the decider of who becomes the leader of this country. That’s what we’re saying,” he added. The activist also criticised the use of insults and the denigration of political opponents as strategies for gaining political power, arguing that such behaviour was not a substitute for presenting credible alternatives to Nigerians. “I’ve never seen in any country where people insult their way to power, where people believe that by denigrating other people, by bending other people’s work to disrepute, will make them preferred,” he said. Awosanya called for more honest conversations about the country’s political choices, insisting that Nigerians should be willing to confront uncomfortable realities rather than excuse conduct that undermines constructive political engagement. nigeria.title: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being ‘cowards’
nigeria.description: At least 66 soldiers in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) have been sentenced to death for cowardice, mutiny and disobeying orders following a military trial in the country’s conflict-hit eastern region, local media have reported. The soldiers were among 71 military personnel tried before a military court in Walikale, North Kivu province. Four were acquitted, while another received a 10-year prison sentence. The Congolese army said the trial was aimed at strengthening discipline among troops fighting armed groups in the east, where years of insecurity have continued to undermine government control. The soldiers were reportedly arrested on October 20 in Walikale after allegedly abandoning their positions and fleeing during clashes with fighters from the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a rebel coalition that includes the M23 group. The army’s operations against armed groups, particularly the M23, have repeatedly been affected by poor discipline and disorganisation within its ranks. The government has consistently accused neighbouring Rwanda of backing the M23, an allegation denied by Kigali and the rebels, despite what has been described as overwhelming evidence. The Congolese military has also faced criticism over its professionalism, while soldiers have complained about poor salaries and inadequate equipment. Last month, another 27 soldiers were sentenced to death on similar charges of cowardice after reportedly withdrawing from frontline positions during clashes with rebels. DR Congo reinstated the death penalty in March 2024 after lifting a moratorium that had been in place for 20 years. The government said the decision was necessary to eliminate “traitors” within the military. Authorities also said capital punishment would apply to individuals involved in armed groups, insurrection, treason and war crimes. The move attracted widespread criticism from human rights organisations. However, no formal executions have been carried out since the death penalty was reinstated. Since the beginning of 2025, at least 507 soldiers have been convicted, including 381 death sentences, according to figures compiled by French broadcaster RFI. In October 2025, former Congolese President Joseph Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia over charges including war crimes and treason. Kabila denied the allegations but did not appear in court to defend himself. He has since been named as the leader of the FRN. nigeria.title: Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO
nigeria.description: Cholera has killed more than 3,000 people worldwide since the start of the year, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, insisting its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remained in reach. The disease killed nearly 7,900 people in 2025, making it “the deadliest year for cholera since 1999”, according to Lorenzo Pezzoli, WHO lead for epidemic-prone bacterial diseases. While data for the first nine months of 2026 show a decline in deaths, more than 3,000 people have still died from the preventable and treatable diarrheal infection, he said, with “nearly nine out of 10 of them in Africa”. The WHO also warned that the current El Nino weather pattern could worsen outbreaks, as cholera can be fuelled by both flooding and water shortages. The UN health agency and the vaccine alliance, Gavi, aim to reduce global cholera cases by 90 percent by 2030 through mass vaccination campaigns and improved access to clean water and sanitation. Although cholera was eliminated from high-income countries generations ago thanks to safe drinking water and modern sewage systems, it can still “kill within a matter of hours” if left untreated, Pezzoli said, despite being “easy and inexpensive to treat” with existing medicines. “The 2030 goal is achievable because the work is already under way,” Pezzoli added, pointing to the International Coordinating Group (ICG) on Vaccine Provision, which last year approved the supply of 71 million doses, funded by Gavi. Vaccines and rapid diagnostic tests are also reaching outbreak zones more quickly, helping health workers detect and respond to infections earlier. WHO and its partners are helping countries identify districts where cholera repeatedly resurfaces and develop response plans. Seven countries — Angola, Bangladesh, the DR Congo, Nigeria, South Sudan, Sudan and Yemen — accounted for about 90 percent of global cases and deaths last year. “The collective response is undeniably bearing fruit, but… it remains insufficient,” Pezzoli said. “We must redouble our efforts to help all these countries reach the elimination goal which means ensuring that, by 2030, cholera no longer poses a public health threat in any of them.” The post Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Trump Media (DJT) Pledges 73% of Its Bitcoin to an Options Program as $1 Billion Note Deadline Nears Trump Media & Technology Group has pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can reuse the coins, the company disclosed in its third-quarter 10-Q filed Monday, three weeks before holders of its $1 billion in convertible notes can demand cash. The Truth Social parent held approximately 15,649 BTC on Sept. 30, Chief Financial Officer Phillip Juhan said on Monday’s earnings call, along with 7 million shares of BlackRock’s IBIT. Of those coins, 11,385.20 were pledged to what the company calls its bitcoin yield management program. The filing says that program requires Trump Media to post bitcoin as collateral “that the counterparty can rehypothecate at their sole discretion.” The pledged coins carried a fair value of $951.4 million at quarter-end. The 10-Q does not name the counterparty. Another 4,260.73 BTC, worth $356.1 million on Sept. 30, sits as collateral for the convertible notes and cannot be withdrawn or distributed until the indenture’s conditions are met. Together, the two buckets account for about 15,646 BTC, nearly all of the stack Juhan described. How the Trump Media options program works Trump Media sells and buys covered calls and puts on bitcoin, settled in bitcoin, to “generate yield on these assets and increase our principal balance of bitcoin,” the filing says. Premiums arrive in bitcoin and are “immediately rehypothecated to our digital asset manager to reinvest.” At quarter-end it had written calls referencing 4,838.40 BTC at strikes from $68,000 to $92,000 and puts on 1,500 BTC at $75,000 to $80,000, all expiring in October. A risk factor spells out the trade-off. The company says its yield counterparties “may not be rated” by credit agencies, that it is limited in its ability to sell or use deployed bitcoin while the arrangements are open, and that where they are unsecured “we may be unable to recover deployed bitcoin in a counterparty insolvency.” Juhan said Trump Media bought 4,359 bitcoin during the quarter with proceeds from a partial sale of its IBIT position, part of a shift toward “third-party institutional” management of its treasury. A $409.7 million profit and a Nov. 30 deadline The bitcoin rally in the third quarter turned Trump Media profitable on paper. Net income was $409.7 million, driven by a $378.1 million gain on digital assets as bitcoin climbed to about $84,000 on Sept. 30 from about $59,000 on June 30. Adjusted EBITDA was still a loss of $12.3 million, and the company lost $234.2 million over the first nine months. Prices have since moved against the stack. With bitcoin near $74,200 Tuesday morning, the 15,649 coins are worth about $1.16 billion, roughly $145 million less than at quarter-end. The bigger test is the notes. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Hyperscale Data (GPUS) Sells Its Last Bitcoin for AI Data Center, Months After Chasing $100 Million Treasury Hyperscale Data has sold the last of its bitcoin, the NYSE American-listed company said Tuesday, unloading about 211.56 BTC for roughly $16 million to pay down debt and fund an AI data center in Michigan. The sales were completed by Nov. 8 at about $76,000 per coin. Since it first sold part of its reserve in late July, Hyperscale has sold approximately 1,113 bitcoin for about $74.4 million, the company said. That works out to an average of roughly $66,800 per coin. At today’s price near $74,200, the same 1,113 BTC would be worth about $82.6 million. The company, which trades under the ticker GPUS, said the money will go toward its Michigan site, where it aims to energize the first 10 megawatts of critical IT capacity in December. “We believe bringing that capacity online is our quickest path to profitability,” CEO Will Horne said in the release. “Selling our Bitcoin reserves reduces our exposure to Bitcoin price swings and gives us cash to pay down debt and fund the work in Michigan. We believe that’s the best use of this capital for all our stockholders.” From a $100 million target to zero The exit is a sharp reversal from Hyperscale’s plans this summer. In late July, the company reported holding more than 1,106 bitcoin and said it wanted to build a $100 million digital asset treasury and reach full parity between its bitcoin holdings and its market capitalization. “Every Bitcoin we acquire further strengthens Hyperscale Data’s balance sheet and expands our financial flexibility,” Executive Chairman Milton “Todd” Ault III said at the time. “We intend to continue building our Bitcoin position over time.” A week later, Hyperscale disclosed its first sale , about 150.5 BTC, leaving it with roughly 958.5 BTC as of Aug. 2, even as its Ault Capital Group subsidiary bought about 15 BTC on the open market. business.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Down Near $73,500 After Hot CPI Print Lifts Fed Hike Bets
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Down Near $73,500 After Hot CPI Print Lifts Fed Hike Bets Bitcoin price traded near $73,500 on Tuesday morning, down about 1% over the past day and roughly $32,000 below its price one year ago, after a hotter-than-expected inflation report revived fears of a larger Federal Reserve rate hike, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The U.S. consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, climbed 0.3% against forecasts for 0.2%. Bitcoin price had been holding near $74,300 in the minutes before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. It dropped to about $73,400 right after the print, briefly undercutting Monday’s overnight low of $73,477 , before steadying in the high-$73,000s. JUST IN: U.S. CPI inflation comes in at 0.4% MoM, higher than expectations Bitcoin falls below $74,000 on the news. pic.twitter.com/Zxq3LtVwAd — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 10, 2026 Food prices jumped 0.5% on the month, energy rose 0.7% and gasoline gained 1.0%. Housing costs increased 0.3%. The report will not carry an annual inflation rate. The government shutdown in October 2025 kept the Bureau of Labor Statistics from collecting a full set of prices, so there is no comparable figure. Bank of America estimated before the release that the annual rates were running near 3.8% for headline and 2.7% for core. Fed hike bets build around the bitcoin price Bond traders moved first. Two- to five-year Treasury yields rose at least 10 basis points on the day after the print, and traders boosted bets on a half-point hike when the Fed meets on Dec. 9. That was the scenario Fed Governor Christopher Waller laid out hours earlier. He said he is “leaning toward” a December increase and would back “more robust action” if inflation ran hotter than expected. “In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Before the data, markets had already largely priced in a quarter-point move. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no yield, and that math has capped the bitcoin price since Friday’s strong jobs report. Bitcoin had already been soft overnight. It lost about 1.4% from midnight UTC before the data, even as Asian markets rallied. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 4.39% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 2.87%, while oil kept falling after President Donald Trump called fresh strikes on Iran “highly unlikely.” Stock futures were mixed going into the release. Dow futures rose 156 points, or 0.3%, while Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.4% after Monday’s rally gave the S&P 500 its best day since April 8. Commodities slipped too. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. sports.title: Mercedes And Williams Tie For Ninth Constructors’ Title In 2026

Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali led the tributes to the team for this major milestone on the track. The win marks a return to the top for Mercedes after a period of struggle. Kimi Antonelli’s record as the youngest ever Drivers’ World Champion coincides with this same season, according to Formula1.com . Winning both titles makes 2026 a historic year for the sport and the Mercedes team. Toto Wolff Joins a Legend The championship victory puts team principal Toto Wolff in rare company. According to Formula 1 Official, his ninth title as a leader draws him level with Sir Frank Williams. Wolff stands alongside Frank in the record books. Domenicali praised the team effort required to reach this point. He stated, “My huge congratulations to everyone at the Mercedes Formula 1 Team on becoming 2026 Constructors’ World Champions. Reaching the summit of Formula 1 is never the achievement of one person alone.” The CEO emphasized that the result came from hundreds of people working together at the factory and the circuit. Every member of the team should feel proud of what they have accomplished this season. Rivals Celebrate Hamilton’s Milestone While the team celebrated, Lewis Hamilton reached a personal milestone with his 400th race start. Fernando Alonso, a rival driver, offered his respects to the veteran on the grid. Alonso noted that Hamilton has had an incredible career in F1, with all 400 races in a very competitive position. Alonso added, “But yes, Lewis obviously has had an incredible career in F1, and 400 races, all of them in a very competitive position. New champion Kimi Antonelli could join that same club as early as 2041. At 24 races a year, the young Italian has a long path ahead if he stays healthy and fast. A New Chapter for the Sport Only Ferrari has more wins with 16, and McLaren sits second with 10. Williams and Mercedes now share the third spot with 9 titles each. Mercedes previously won the title for eight consecutive seasons from 2014 to 2021. The 2026 win breaks a recent run where McLaren claimed the 2024 and 2025 titles. A Mercedes-powered car has secured the championship for the third year in a row. Domenicali concluded the official remarks by noting the significance of the moment. He said, “Mercedes have returned to the very top, and in doing so have written another remarkable chapter in the history of Formula 1.” The wait for another Constructors’ Championship ended last weekend in Sao Paulo.

sports.title: Agent confirms Liverpool star is in talks over new deal
sports.description: Agent confirms Liverpool star is in talks over new deal Alisson Becker Contract Talks Give Liverpool a Clear Goalkeeping Decision Liverpool have a decision to make on Alisson Becker, and it looks like the process has already started. Early discussions are underway over a new deal for the Brazilian, whose current contract is due to expire next June. That matters, because Alisson remains one of the few players in this squad who can still decide games on his own. Liverpool know it, Alisson knows it, and now his camp have effectively confirmed it in public. Alisson Becker open to Liverpool stay There has been noise around several Liverpool contracts in recent months, including Alexis Mac Allister, but Alisson’s situation is simpler. He wants to stay. His agent, Ze Maria, made that clear, saying to WinWin : “Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.” That is not a deal done, and it is not even close to one yet. Still, when a player is happy, the agent is talking and the club are engaged, it usually means there is something concrete to discuss. Photo: IMAGO Liverpool contract talks hinge on age and value The issue is not quality. Alisson has delivered that for years. The issue is age and cost. He is 34, and Liverpool have not built a reputation for handing major renewals to players in that bracket. Then again, rules in football tend to bend for elite players. Liverpool already made one such call when they renewed Mohamed Salah’s deal in April 2025. Alisson could fall into the same category, particularly if the club believe there is still another season or two of top-level performance there. His current wages are reported at £250,000 per week, which already places him among the top earners in the squad. Any extension would involve another serious financial commitment. That is the real calculation here. Crystal Palace display showed Alisson quality Recent mistakes had raised a few questions, fairly enough, but his display against Crystal Palace was a reminder of why Liverpool have trusted him for so long. He made a series of high-level saves and looked like himself again, calm, sharp and decisive. That is why this conversation is happening. If Alisson were declining badly, there would be no serious debate. Instead, Liverpool are weighing cost against certainty, and in his position certainty carries a premium. Nothing is settled yet. These are early talks. But the signs are positive, and for Liverpool, keeping Alisson Becker may still be the most sensible piece of business available.

sports.title: Official | Vincent Kompany returns to work at Bayern Munich
sports.description: Official | Vincent Kompany returns to work at Bayern Munich Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has taken another significant step towards returning to the touchline following his recent health scare. The Bundesliga champions confirmed on Tuesday that the 40-year-old Belgian has returned to the club’s Säbener Straße training facility. Kompany has been absent from his coaching duties since collapsing while observing a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team on October 23. He was subsequently hospitalised, with further medical examinations reportedly revealing an irritation of the meninges. Bayern have now confirmed that their head coach is recovering and has been back at the club’s training facilities since the beginning of the week. Kompany is also undergoing rehabilitation for a shoulder injury. According to the Münchener Tageszeitung , the Belgian was back working at his office computer by approximately 10 a.m. on Tuesday morning. Vincent Kompany could return after international break Bayern have not yet confirmed when Kompany will resume his responsibilities on the touchline. However, honorary president Uli Hoeneß suggested during an appearance on Bayerischer Rundfunk’s Sonntags-Stammtisch that the coach could return following the November international break. This would potentially put Kompany in contention to oversee Bayern’s Bundesliga encounter with 1. FC Cologne on November 20. In Kompany’s absence, assistant coach Aaron Danks has overseen first-team affairs, with Bayern winning all five competitive fixtures during that period. GGFN | Peter Weis

The greatest goal scorer in NHL history will be calling it a career this year, as Alex Ovechkin has announced this will be his final season in the NHL. The Washington Capitals ’ star announced the decision before the team’s home opener this year. As Ovechkin prepares for retirement, other teams have celebrated him , giving gifts to the Great 8 as he visits their city one final time. Ovechkin and the Capitals hope that he will get to lift the Stanley Cup one more time before his career ends. Regardless of the outcome of this season, the greatest goal scorer of all time will be heading to Toronto for induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame at some point down the road. The biggest question is: when will it happen? Traditionally, players have to wait three years to be eligible, but there is the possibility that the Hall of Fame could waive the waiting period , something Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic explored. “And Alex Ovechkin? He has announced this will be his final NHL season, and some have wondered if the Hockey Hall of Fame should waive its three-year waiting period for the all-time NHL goals leader, as it did for players like Gordie Howe, Mario Lemieux and Wayne Gretzky,” LeBrun wrote. First of all, the bylaw provision that gave the Hockey Hall of Fame Board of Directors the authority to waive the three-year waiting period was eliminated after Gretzky was elected in 1999. I think the rationale at the time was that it’s better for the inductee to be removed from the spotlight for a ‘reflection period’ after their career. sports.title: Tom Brady calls out what current NFL players are ‘really missing’ compared to his generation
sports.description: L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images NFL legend Tom Brady has suggested that modern athletes are ‘really missing’ someone to challenge them every day to be their best. Brady was selected in the sixth round of the 2000 NFL draft by the New England Patriots, perhaps suggesting at the time that he would not go on to become one of the best players in history. However, he worked hard throughout his career to cement his legacy. But he has now questioned ‘Who’s challenging’ the new generation of players to be their very best. In a video shared on X/Twitter , he said: “We would play in any weather and we were challenged every day to be our best, too. And I think that’s maybe what the modern athletes [are] really missing. “Who’s challenging those kids to be their very best? Not who’s paying for their lunch money that day or who’s paying for the sponsorship. “It’s like who’s making that person a better, more complete athlete, at the end of every game. And that’s what I appreciate about coaching and organisations that push our players to be better.” Brady is one of the most decorated players in the history of the sport and holds the record for the most Super Bowl wins (7). After an initial retirement in 2022, he confirmed in February 2023 that his NFL career was over for good. sports.description: Grêmio aim to clear injury list and keep momentum against the bottom four After securing a place in the Copa do Brasil final and enjoying three days off, Grêmio's squad returns to training this Wednesday (11). sports.title: Bickerstaff Makes His Stance on Cade Cunningham Clear
sports.description: Detroit Pistons superstar guard Cade Cunningham was on the floor for only 26:31 against the Washington Wizards on Monday night. He picked up his fifth personal foul in the third quarter and did not return until midway through the fourth , finishing with 17 points on 43.8 percent shooting from the field in a 122-111 win for Detroit. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff was asked what Cunningham does so well, in comments reported by Hunter Patterson of The Athletic . Bickerstaff said, “He just needs to be himself. Cade has been amazing since we’ve been here at understanding the moment and doing what’s right in the moment. He’s always put the team first, so this isn’t going to be about him doing something for him. It’s going to be what the game deems necessary and how (defenses) decide to defend him.” Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives past Los Angeles Lakers forward Jake LaRavia (12) in the first half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Cade Cunningham shaped the Pistons win in other ways Even with the 17 points, Cunningham grabbed three rebounds, recorded seven assists and added one steal. He is about making the right play for his teammates and getting them involved. Cunningham is averaging 22.3 points and 7.6 assists per game this season, and that assist average ranks ninth in the NBA . The number is down from the 9.9 assists per game he posted last season, but Cunningham is still willing to share the basketball with his teammates. Detroit has needed that playmaking more than usual. Center Jalen Duren, who has been out since late October, will miss at least two more weeks with a right hamstring strain, the Pistons said Sunday, and that latest Duren update leaves Cunningham setting up a reshuffled frontcourt. Three Pistons outscored Cunningham against Washington Duncan Robinson and Daniss Jenkins each scored 22 points in the game for Detroit, and Jenkins added eight assists. As for John Collins, he led the Pistons with 24 points and 10 rebounds against the Wizards. Detroit needed all of it. Washington’s Anthony Davis went for 44 points and 13 rebounds and the Pistons still pulled away. It was good to see other players on this team be able to contribute and help out Cunningham. It is one of the reasons why the Pistons are off to a 7-3 start this NBA season.

sports.description: Jaguars make Brian Thomas Jr. trade decision after major Monday deals originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars are the NFL's biggest spender at this year's NFL trade deadline. While the Chicago Bears have spent two first-round picks already, the Jaguars have made the most moves of note so far. All on Monday before deadline day, James Gladstone acquired Jessie Bates III, Davon Godchaux, and Jordan Davis to get some massive upgrades on the defensive side of the ball. Now, the focus shifts to wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and if he's traded or not. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Jaguars have made their decision: Thomas is staying put. Jacksonville has told NFL teams as much, with Thomas now set to remain with the Jaguars as they pursue a Super Bowl title. Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. despite trade speculation "The Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources," Fowler reports. "They have relayed that to interested teams." While there was bound to be plenty of interest in Thomas from teams like the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers , the Jaguars are electing to keep Thomas this season. After adding Jordan Davis in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles and Jessie Bates III in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons , deciding to keep Thomas through the trade deadline is a sensible decision for the Jaguars. They're all-in, and Thomas should help in some way. It's not a major surprise, especially considering that the Jaguars are trying to win it all this year, and trading Thomas to a potential playoff opponent wouldn't make sense. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Besides, if the Jaguars were to lose Parker Washington or Jakobi Meyers to injury, not having Thomas at their disposal would be a major blow. Even though Thomas might be third on the depth chart at best, with Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter also being involved, the Jaguars are better off keeping him in hopes Thomas can provide any value down the stretch for their Super Bowl push. The trade value for Thomas was also likely not good enough to convince the Jaguars to move him, as it might've been hard for the Jaguars to get a second-round pick for Thomas, and a third-rounder might not have been a lock either. For a Super Bowl contender, keeping a WR like Thomas is a perfectly reasonable decision to make. While WR-needy teams might've wished they had moved Thomas, for the Jaguars, keeping him is the right call for the 2026 season. But a disastrous summer began to turn the tide away from him, before a broken collarbone at the Sachsenring left him facing an uphill battle to get his campaign back on track. Despite that setback, the points cushion Bezzecchi had built earlier in the season meant he remained firmly in the title fight after the summer break. A consistent run of results in August further helped his cause. But a crash while fighting for the lead in Misano proved to be the final nail in the coffin, leaving his championship hopes effectively at the mercy of his rivals. Even when Bezzecchi returned to the top step of the podium in Indonesia, his victory owed more to Raul Fernandez’s physical limitations than his own pace. The impression was that the Italian was slowly chipping towards the front while recovering from the injury, but was still some way off the level that had made him the early favourite for the 2026 crowd. The Qatar Grand Prix, however, showed that he had lost none of his outright speed, and he can still leave his rivals in his wake when he is comfortable on the bike. Perhaps not coincidentally, Bezzecchi failed to score in the restarted sprint after making a poor launch from pole and later colliding with Marc Marquez at Turn 1. The same sprint weakness that had plagued him early in the season resurfaced, even if neither rider was to blame for the incident that left Bezzecchi on the ground. technology.title: Fireworks AI gets burned twice as customer data exposure widens
technology.description: Fireworks AI has disclosed another cyberattack in October and a wider customer data exposure involving billing records, datasets, and incomplete model weights. The company, which lets customers train and run AI models, said a third-party cloud provider hosting its research and development machines was compromised on October 23. Attackers used that access the following day to reach Fireworks development systems and run an unauthorized workload. Fireworks suspects links to financially motivated criminals involved in LLMJacking – selling unauthorized access to AI models through illicit gateways. Fireworks grouped the affected data into three categories: Resource metadata: Resource identifiers, display names, descriptions, creation times, and more Billing information: Billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment histories, account balances, and credit usages. Payment card numbers are not saved and therefore unaffected Model weights and datasets: For certain customers, a subset of incomplete model weights and datasets were accessed, Fireworks said Lin Qiao, Fireworks co-founder and CEO, said the apparent motive was not stealing model weights in response to concerns raised by Cantina Security CEO Hari Mulackal. "From what we see attackers are not after weights," said Qiao. "Most downloads were partial and stopped." Render founder and CEO Anurag Goel shared a notification from Notion warning that some chats with its AI assistant may have been exposed through the Fireworks incident. "Following an investigation by the Notion security team, we have determined that your workspace, Render, was among the <1 percent of Notion workspaces that may have been affected by the Fireworks security incident," the email sent to Goel stated. "Some unattributable chat sessions with Notion AI may have been exposed in this incident." Notion said the exposed transcripts lacked separate information linking them to particular users or workspaces. As Reddit users pointed out , however, the conversations themselves could contain identifying details. "Beyond what's in the chat transcript itself, there's no information tying the chat back to your workspace, users, or company," the email added. technology.title: FDA warns GLP-1 drugs may pose risk of rare condition that causes vision loss
technology.description: The Food and Drug Administration is warning that popular obesity drugs—including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro—may carry a "potential increased risk" of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss. In a drug safety communication Monday , the FDA said it will now require makers of GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs to add a warning about that risk on their drug labels. The specific eye condition it warns of is called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy or NAION . The condition is caused by restricted blood flow to the optic nerve, which leads to swelling and cell death and ultimately damages the nerve, causing abrupt vision loss that can often be permanent. It's unknown how GLP-1 drugs may cause NAION. The condition is rare overall, occurring in somewhere between two and 10 people in 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmologists. These small numbers have made it more difficult to determine with certainty if there is a connection. Further complicating the potential link is the fact that the risk factors for developing NAION are common among patients taking GLP-1 drugs. But it's nonetheless a worthwhile exercise for those who haven't been paying close attention to the development of machine learning over the past few years and for policymakers who may benefit from a review of AI's metastatic growth. "The last five years constitute a watershed moment in the history of AI," said Professor Sheila McIlraith, chair of the AI100 Standing Committee, in a statement. " This report examines what led to the extraordinary capabilities of today's AI systems, and how they are reshaping society. As we look ahead, we anticipate continued increase in AI capabilities alongside transformative advances in science and medicine. Established in 2014, the One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI100) is overseen by a Standing Committee of AI experts and administered by Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). science.title: Curiosity Mars rover sizes up new 'Nazca' dig site | Space photo of the day for Nov. 10, 2026
science.description: null NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager, showing the abundance of disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, dubbed "Nazca." (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it. What is it? Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target. MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image. Why is it incredible? Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow. The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

This 35 by 35 target is based on analysis by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) on what is needed to keep the 1.5°C global warming target within reach. Currently, electricity is estimated to make up just 23.4 per cent of the energy delivered to consumers, known as final energy – a figure that has increased by only 6.7 percentage points since 2000. This means that hitting the target will require the rate of electrification to quadruple compared with the first quarter of the 21st century and triple compared with the rate between 2020 and 2025. Judit Hecke at New Climate Institute, a German think tank, says such an acceleration is possible but “the challenge is getting policies, investment and infrastructure moving at the same pace”. Advertisement Progress on renewable energy has been encouraging, with renewables making up a higher proportion of overall electricity production year after year, and renewable capacity additions have been setting new records each year. In 2024, the most recent IRENA data, nearly 32 per cent of global electricity production came from renewable sources compared with just 18 per cent in 2000. Renewable energy capacity has increased from 0.8 terawatts in 2000 to 5.2 terawatts in 2025. But this is a long way from the COP28 pledge for UN member states to reach 11 terawatts of renewable capacity by 2030. However, Hecke points out that the electrification target includes electricity regardless of how it is generated, meaning that a country could make progress while still heavily relying on coal and gas in the power sector.
